$$
A={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}^{T},
$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =-4.$ Computing $A-(-4)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+4I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 4 & 4\end{aligned}]+4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],
$$

where $‖v‖=\sqrt{5}.$ Dividing $v$ by its norm, we obtain the normalized eigenvector: 

$$
u=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, the required orthogonal projection matrix is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-ebade115-5b0c-52d7-94cc-8ec9e5babad9"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $$

$$

where ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}$ and ${\lambda }_{2},$ respectively.

Moreover, ${u}_{i}\cdot {u}_{i}^{T}$ is the projection matrix corresponding to ${u}_{i}.$

First, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to $\lambda =-4.$ Computing $A-(-4)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+4I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 4 & 4\end{aligned}]+4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot {u}^{T} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

Specifically, if $\mathbf{u}_i$ denotes an orthonormal eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda_i$ for $i=1,\ldots, n$, then

$$A=\sum_{i=1}^n \lambda_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{u}_i^T.$$

Expressing a symmetric matrix $A$ in this way is called the **spectral decomposition** of $A.$

To demonstrate, let's find the spectral decomposition of the $2\times 2$ symmetric matrix $A,$ given by

$$A = [\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].$$

The eigenvalues of $A$ are $\lambda_1 = 6$ and $\lambda_2 = -4,$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are

$$\mathbf{v}_1 = [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \quad \textrm{and} \quad \mathbf{v}_2 = [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$$

The spectral decomposition of $A$ is given by

$$A =\sum_{i=1}^2 \lambda_i \mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{u}_i^T = \lambda_1 \mathbf u_1 \mathbf u_1^T + \lambda_2 \mathbf u_2 \mathbf u_2^T,$$

where $\mathbf u_1$ and $\mathbf u_2$ are orthonormal eigenvectors of $A$ corresponding to $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2,$ respectively.

First, let's normalize our eigenvectors:

$$\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {u}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the spectral decomposition of $A$ is

$$\begin{aligned}A & ={\lambda }_{1}{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}+{\lambda }_{2}{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T} \\ & =6\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-4)\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\ & =6\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 3\end{aligned}]+(-4)\cdot \frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\ & ={{6}_{⏟}}_{{\lambda }_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10} & \frac{3}{10} \\ \frac{3}{10} & \frac{9}{10}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{u}_{1}{u}_{1}^{T}}+{{(-4)}_{⏟}}_{{\lambda }_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{10} & -\frac{3}{10} \\ -\frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{u}_{2}{u}_{2}^{T}}.\end{aligned}$$

In this decomposition, the matrix $\mathbf{u}_i \mathbf{u}_i^T$ is the orthogonal projection matrix that maps any $\mathbf x \in \mathbb R^2$ onto the subspace spanned by $\mathbf u_i.$" :tutorial/id
